title: Every Function Splits into an Even Part and an Odd Part
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Let f be any function whose domain is symmetric about the origin. Define E(x) = [f(x) + f(-x)]/2 and O(x) = [f(x) - f(-x)]/2. Prove that f(x) = E(x) + O(x), that E is even, that O is odd, and that this decomposition is unique.

steps.title: Verify the Decomposition Identity
steps.explanation: Adding the two definitions term by term, the f(-x) contributions appear with opposite signs and cancel, leaving exactly f(x).
steps.why: The plus/minus pairing is engineered so that the reflected terms annihilate; only 2*f(x)/2 survives.

steps.title: Show E is Even
steps.explanation: Replace x by -x in the definition of E: the two summands simply exchange places, so the value is unchanged.
steps.why: Addition is commutative, so f(-x)+f(x) equals f(x)+f(-x); this is precisely the condition E(-x) = E(x) for evenness.

steps.title: Show O is Odd
steps.explanation: Substituting -x into O swaps the order of the subtraction, which flips the overall sign of the expression.
steps.why: Reversing a difference negates it: b - a = -(a - b); hence O(-x) = -O(x), the defining property of an odd function.

steps.title: Prove Uniqueness of the Split
steps.explanation: If f = E1 + O1 for any even E1 and odd O1, then f(-x) = E1(x) - O1(x). Adding and subtracting the two equations forces E1 and O1 to be exactly the E and O constructed above.
steps.why: The pair of equations in the unknowns E1(x) and O1(x) is a 2-by-2 linear system with a unique solution, so no other even-odd split can exist.
